reading.body:
Michael Chappell is named on 84 AI lobbying filings, and the largest single client block is not a technology company but the Recording Industry Association of America, at 14 filings.

The client list is the useful part. Media and copyright interests lead at 14 and 12 filings, an industry association follows at 9, and the technology names arrive lower and thinner: TSMC Arizona at 7, Cisco at 6, Siemens at 5, Oracle and Siemens Energy at 4 each, Apple and Anthropic at 3 each. One lobbyist carrying both the Recording Industry Association of America and Anthropic is the pattern worth noting, because it means the same person is positioned on both sides of the copyright fight that governs what AI models may be trained on.

The filings also name three bills, HR 7757, S 2750 and S 3150, all from 2025 or later. The data does not say what those bills contain, whether Chappell lobbied for or against them, or what positions were taken. It records that he was listed on filings that name them.

What this does not cover is outcome. A filing is a disclosure that lobbying occurred, not evidence that it changed anything. The counts measure how often a client appears on filings that mention AI, not spending, not intensity, and not influence. The prior government position is disclosed because the Lobbying Disclosure Act requires covered positions from the prior twenty years to be listed, and that is all the data says about it.
